sources.title: Anode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries, from Conventional Materials to High-Entropy Oxides: A Review of Synthesis Methods, Properties and Sustainability Challenges

materials.name: High entropy oxide rock salt mixture

evidence.text_snippet: Yin et al. [78] present the sol–gel synthesis of Al-doped, carbon-coated Li4Ti5O12 (LTO) anodes, leveraging the method's ability to produce homogenous, nano-sized particles with uniform doping and carbon coating.
reports the sol–gel synthesis of Li3VO4/carbon (Li3VO4/C) composites for use as anode materials in lithium-ion batteries.

Courtel et al. [80] reported the hydrothermal synthesis of ultra-fine ZnMn2O4 nanoparticles (≤5 nm) as high-performance anode materials for Li-ion batteries. The hydrothermal method, using ethylene glycol as a solvent enabled precise control over particle size and prevented agglomeration
Li et al. [81] reported in their study the synthesis of nitrogen-doped TiO2/reduced graphene oxide (N-TiO2/rGO) hybrids via a hydrothermal approach, employing thiourea as the nitrogen source.
Shen et al. [82] obtained ZnO-loaded porous carbon (ZnO/PC) composites for the first time via a facile solvothermal method.
Gu et al. [85] used in their work the co-precipitation synthesis to obtain MgCo2O4-coated Li4Ti5O12 (LTO) composite anodes for lithium-ion batteries.
Birrozzi et al. [90] explored the use of flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) for the synthesis of Li4Ti5O12 (LTO) nanoparticles
Laurenti et al. [91] demonstrate in their work the chemical vapor deposition growth of ZnO nanostructures directly onto stainless steel current collectors
Kim et al. [95] obtained Ni-doped SnO2–carbon nanofiber (CNF) composites via electrospinning and carbonization

Kim et al. [95] obtained Ni-doped SnO2–carbon nanofiber (CNF) composites via electrospinning and carbonization, resulting in uniformly distributed 15 nm SnO2/NiO nanoparticles embedded on conductive CNFs.
followed by carbonization in a vacuum and reported by Gu and his co-workers [96].
Fe3O4/C composite fibers were also synthesized by the electrospinning method, followed by carbonization in a vacuum and reported by Gu and his co-workers [96].
Researchers have synthesized spinel HEO nanoparticles, (Cr0.2Mn0.2Co0.2Ni0.2Zn0.2)3O4, using a solution combustion method.
On the other hand, the porous spinel-phase HEO, (Cr0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2Zn0.2)3O4, was synthesized at low temperatures using a sol–gel method.
